I think it's important to ask these questions and think critically about choices like this. But in this particular case, I end up being OK with it. Piggybacking off what another commenter said, the casting of the actress as the daughter of the action star (mixed race) and the other actress (white) seems plausible to me. Would it be *nice* if they had cast someone with more of a mixed race look? Sure. But personally I don't think this disaster movie is guilty of the same kind or level of offense as another film, not by a LONG shot. (And I'm not just talking about a specific actress here.)

What if a well-known actress best fits the role the director was aiming for? What if all the mixed Asian actresses auditioning just didn't quite capture the right mood for the movie?

The odds of that are extremely low. The idea that not a single mixed Asian actress could have done as good of a job as the well-known actress -- in portraying a mixed Asian character, no less -- is fairly preposterous. And I say this as a big fan of hers.

But even if it WERE true, how about all the other characters? How is it possible that a movie set in a tropical location can star an entirely white cast? I think that's why this grates so much. If the well-known actress were just one -- or even one of a couple -- white characters amidst an otherwise racially representative film, I don't think you'd hear as much criticism.

And frankly, if they had at least dyed her hair, I personally might be less annoyed. But they made ZERO effort to be conscious or considerate of the racial/cultural field they were playing in. That, to me, cannot be overlooked.

Hm, okay, it's possible I'm being unfairly influenced by the fact that (1) the actress looks so much like she could be the other actress's child, and (2) the actor is relatively light-skinned and ambiguously ethnic. I'll give it some more thought.

Regardless of that, I maintain that even if casting the first actress for a mixed race role is as bad as casting the second actress for one, the cultural/racial problems in that film are much larger than those in the other film. See my comment on this thread: [link].

So I think the larger context is at play for me too, whether that's fair or not.

I really don't think there was anything special that my friends needed as mixed-heritage boys, versus me as a mixed-heritage girl...
